item.title: 'My captain Shreyas, my coach Ricky': Hardik Pandya's first comment after joining Punjab Kings
item.description: NEW DELHI: Hardik Pandya has made his first public comment after joining Punjab Kings (PBKS) ahead of the 2027 IPL season. Pandya has moved from Mumbai Indians (MI) to Punjab Kings for Rs 18 crore. In return, PBKS have traded fast bowler Arshdeep Singh to MI. The trade has been completed ahead of the 2027 IPL season. Pandya's new fee of Rs 18 crore is higher than his earlier fee of Rs 16.35 crore. Arshdeep has moved to MI at his existing fee of Rs 18 crore, according to an IPL statement. The all-rounder shared a message on Instagram, mentioning his new captain Shreyas Iyer, coach Ricky Ponting and the team. "Sat Sri Akal. My Captain. Shreyas. My Coach. Ricky. My team. All of Punjab. I am standing behind you," Pandya wrote. The move brings an end to Pandya's second stint with Mumbai Indians, where he won four IPL titles. Pandya first joined MI in 2015 and played a key role in their title-winning campaigns in 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020. He returned to the franchise in 2024 and took over as captain from Rohit Sharma. item.title: Joe Lacob talks Juste Jocyte’s future after Natalie Nakase drama
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Golden State Valkyries owner Joe Lacob isn’t shutting the door on Juste Jocyte. Juste Jocyte didn’t bite her tongue after spending basically the entire WNBA Finals glued to the pine, seeing just six total minutes on the floor. The 20-year-old made her feelings known in an interview with the Lithuanian media, making it clear she was miserable with how Natalie Nakase used her. Now, heading into the offseason, Jocyte is putting the Valkyries front office on notice, telling them she has zero interest in riding the bench next year, and she won’t stick around without real minutes. Joe Lacob issues an update on Juste Jocyte’s future Joe Lacob is trying to play damage control before the situation spirals. Instead of taking the bait and firing back at Jocyte’s comments, the Valkyries owner is playing the long game, making it clear he doesn’t want to let the 20-year-old walk away. He said: “I kind of understand she’s competitive and would like to win and didn’t play. But she’s also only 20. We had a pretty great roster, very deep. I think she can be a very good player and we’d really love to have her back. “So I think she will certainly earn a lot more playing time in the future. She didn’t get to play as much as she wanted to, and that’s understandable. “I think she can be a very good player and we would really love to have her back.” Even with Lacob trying to play nice, it’s hard to picture Jocyte sticking around in the Bay. That bridge with Nakase is burned, and Golden State isn’t about to let locker room bad blood poison the culture they’re building. Once trust is shot, a clean break is the only realistic way out. item.title: MCC to introduce Spirit of Cricket Award at ILT20 Season 5
item.description: The Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) will introduce a Spirit of Cricket Award at the ILT20 Season 5, recognising a team or individual who best reflects the game's values during the tournament, which begins in the UAE on November 21. The award will be presented at the end of the competition on December 20, marking the first such recognition at the six-team T20 league. MCC, the guardian of cricket's Laws, will work with the tournament organisers to promote sportsmanship and fair play among players. The partnership is part of MCC's wider effort to promote the Spirit of Cricket across the game. The Club has previously worked with ICC Europe to present similar awards at three men's sub-regional World Cup qualification events earlier this year. Rob Lynch, MCC's Director of Cricket and Operations, said franchise leagues could play an important role in setting standards for player behaviour. “MCC sees franchise leagues as the standard-bearers for playing the game in the right way – playing hard but playing fair and with a smile on your face,” Lynch said. He added that the competitive nature of franchise cricket, where international team-mates often face each other, could help improve conduct across the sport. Mike Fordham, Interim Chief Operating Officer of the ILT20, said the partnership aligned with the league's emphasis on sporting values. He also pointed to the participation of players from 19 cricketing nations across its six franchises this season. “The tournament has always been hugely competitive with top quality cricket on display. Our matches have always been played in the right spirit with cricket’s traditional sporting values remaining at the forefront,” Fordham said. Season 5 will run from November 21 to December 20, with matches scheduled at the Sheikh Zayed Cricket Stadium in Abu Dhabi, Dubai International Stadium and Sharjah Cricket Stadium. Defending champions Desert Vipers will be joined by Gulf Giants, MI Emirates, Dubai Capitals, Abu Dhabi Knight Riders and Sharjah Warriorz in the 34-match competition. Previous winners include Gulf Giants, MI Emirates and Dubai Capitals. The new recognition will be separate from the main MCC Spirit of Cricket Award, established by MCC and the BBC in 2013 in honour of Christopher Martin-Jenkins.

item.description: Chelsea right-back Malo Gusto open to January transfer Chelsea right-back Malo Gusto (23) is open to leaving Chelsea in the January transfer window, according to the BBC . The France international is far from being a guaranteed starter in West London. Since Xabi Alonso’s appointment at Chelsea FC, Gusto’s playign time has dramatically decreased. item.title: Robert Horry Rips Walker Kessler’s Offensive Game: “Guys In Elementary Got Better Post Moves Than Him”
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers have the NBA’s best record at 10-2, and new arrival Walker Kessler has played his part in their early success. Kessler has impressed on defense, and former Laker Robert Horry likes what he has seen from the big man on that end of the floor. What Horry, who won three titles with the Lakers, doesn’t like, though, is Kessler’s offensive game, and he urged him to improve on the Big Shot Bob Podcast . “You know what’s really scary about Walker Kessler?” Horry said. “Hey, I know guys in elementary got better post moves than him. He got no post moves, man. I’m like, who is teaching this dude any post moves? You’re seven f***ing feet tall. Get you a little jump hook, man. You don’t have to dunk everything.” Kessler really doesn’t have a reliable post move. The 25-year-old is primarily a rim-runner, and if you are good at that next to Luka Doncic , you’ll score some points. Kessler is averaging 14.9 points, 10.8 rebounds, 1.7 assists, 1.3 steals, and 2.3 blocks per game for the Lakers in 2026-27. Over 60 percent of his field goal attempts have been within three feet of the basket, and only 1.8 percent have come from beyond 10 feet. Now, Kessler showed off some range in the 2025-26 season for the Utah Jazz . He went 6-8 from three in five games before needing season-ending shoulder surgery. So, when the Lakers acquired Kessler, the No. 22 pick in the 2022 NBA Draft, from the Jazz in the summer, the expectation was that he’d be a threat from beyond the arc. He even shared that head coach JJ Redick wanted him to shoot more threes , but he hasn’t even attempted a single one through 12 games. “I don’t even think he wants to score ’cause I’ve seen him get offensive rebounds and kick that b***h out instead of crunching that b***h,” Horry said. “… I’m like, dude, you 7 ft tall. Get you a power dribble. Go up and dunk that b***h too. Like [Shaquille O’Neal], you monkey dunk that b***h. That’s what he said. That’s what Shaq used to say. So dunk on somebody and then just move on. “That’s what I want him to do and stop kicking that b***h out ’cause you don’t get no plays ran for you,” Horry added. Now, teams like the player who gets the offensive rebound to kick it out for an open three. That could well be the case here, but we don’t know for sure. While Kessler isn’t the perfect offensive center, that wasn’t why the Lakers gave him a four-year, $130 million contract and gave up two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps to the Jazz. They wanted a rim runner and a defensive anchor, and he is just that. “He’s a great shot blocker,” Horry said. “And the thing I like about Kessler the best is he goes after everything. And even though he’s gotten dunked on a couple times, he don’t give a s***… He’s still going to go out and try to block. item.title: Top 2027 recruit Amaya Manuel commits to Tennessee
item.description: Top 2027 recruit Amaya Manuel has committed to Tennessee , she announced. The 5-8 point guard from Saint Louis (MO) Lift For Life Academy chose the Lady Vols over programs including Missouri and Arkansas. “Definitely a family type of environment,” she previously told Rivals of factors she was considering. “I want to do a lot of team bonding and stuff. I really want to have a good relationship with all the teammates and all my coaches. I also want a program that’s big on development for each player. You know, let me do what I what I can do, not limiting me, but making me better.” Tennessee earned the last official visit and the commitment. The Lady Vols are getting a strong point guard in Manuel. “My biggest strength is definitely driving,” she said. “I just came back from my ACL injury in November, so I’m just now coming back, but I’ve always been able to drive and be aggressive. I’m trying to get back to that. I still think that’s my strength, but I need to get better at that now.” Manuel marks Tennessee’s second commitment in the 2027 class after adding versatile wing Maci Pringle.

item.title: JJ Gabriel set to sign Real Madrid contract by early next week – report
item.description: JJ Gabriel set to sign Real Madrid contract by early next week – report Real Madrid are expected to complete the signing of Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel by the beginning of next week, with the 16-year-old’s move to the Spanish capital approaching its final stages. According to journalist Ben Fernandes Santos , the agreement is close to being finalised, with the teenager having made his preference clear to the European clubs interested in securing his signature. It is to be noted that Gabriel attracted attention across Europe following his decision to leave Manchester United in September. Real Madrid, after tough negotiations and a fight with other suitors, emerged as his preferred destination, with Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain among the clubs previously linked with the highly-rated forward. Manchester United fail to convince JJ Gabriel to stay Manchester United reportedly made several attempts to change Gabriel’s mind, with club executives and manager Michael Carrick holding discussions with the player and his representatives. Real Madrid could announce JJ Gabriel’s signing by next week. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images) However, those efforts did not alter his intention to pursue a move to Real Madrid. The teenager requested to leave United in September and has since been training independently in Spain while his future is being resolved. His decision became clearer when he was asked to choose between Barcelona and Real Madrid . “Obviously, Real Madrid,” he said. As reported before, Real Madrid had reached a verbal agreement with the teenager and were confident of signing him. However, formal club-to-club negotiations had not yet taken place until a few weeks back. Real Madrid have a clear development plan Real Madrid have won the race for JJ Gabriel. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images) Real Madrid are understood to want Gabriel to begin his development with Castilla , allowing him to experience senior football while remaining close to the first-team environment. The Spanish club believe their pathway offers an attractive opportunity for the teenager to progress towards the senior squad. His representative, Ali Barat, has been involved in discussions over the move, while reports have also suggested that Jose Mourinho played a role in convincing Gabriel that Madrid would be the right destination. All in all, Real Madrid are set to sign the highly-rated teenager, and the official announcement could be arriving soon.

Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images The College Football Playoff selection committee released its second rankings on Tuesday night , placing Georgia at No. 1 after their dominant 42-7 win over Ole Miss. The top spot changed hands, while Miami dropped six places to No. 7 despite losing by only a touchdown. This week’s list shows massive movement across the board, with no team staying in the same position as last week. Georgia, Notre Dame, and the Bruins all saw their stock rise significantly following recent results. UCLA moved up four spots to No. 4 after a 34-20 victory over Minnesota. The Bruins are now one of only two unbeaten teams left in major college football, joining Utah at No. 2. Indiana suffered a steep fall, dropping five spots to No. 9 despite not playing last weekend. The committee chair said the shift was a correction based on new data from the weekend’s games. Why the Top Spot Changed Hands Georgia took over No. 1 ranking after blowing out Mississippi on Nov. 7. The Bulldogs had lost the top spot the week before, but their performance in Oxford, Miss., erased any doubt about their status. Hunter Yurachek, who leads the 13-person selection committee, said the move reflected the team’s strength rather than an admission of error from the previous week. Georgia’s defense and offense both looked strong enough to handle any opponent in the 12-team playoff format. Notre Dame also made a big jump, rising six spots to No. 5. The Irish leapfrogged Miami after beating the Hurricanes last weekend. Notre Dame’s win proved that the Irish could handle a top-tier opponent on the road. The committee rewarded the Irish for their resilience and their ability to close out a tough game against a rival. The Miami Drop and the UCLA Rise Miami’s fall to No. 7 was the most painful result for fans of the Canes. They lost by a single touchdown on the road and were missing their best player, Malachi Toney. The injury to Toney likely hurt their game planning and execution. item.description: Most years, the No. 1 recruit in NCAA men’s golf is up for discussion. This year, there is no debate. Miles Russell isn’t just the unquestioned top-ranked player in the Class of 2027 as the week-long early signing period starts Wednesday; the 18-year-old from Jacksonville Beach, Florida, might be the best college prospect in over a decade. He will sign with the Florida State Seminoles, who also have the No. 1 class, which includes top European recruit Edwin Askerfors, Tiger Woods’ son Charlie Woods and instate product Kaden Puranik. Close behind its rival is Florida, which inks Nos. 2 and 3 in the class, Jessy Huebner and Giuseppe Puebla. North Carolina also boasts two top-10 signees in No. 5 Dawson Lew and No. 9 Evan Liu. Most shocking, though, was Asterisk Talley, the top-ranked girls junior, not signing with Stanford for now. Talley remains committed as she weighs her options, leaving the Cardinal to sign only No. 2 Anna Fang. That knocks Stanford down to the No. 4 class behind No. 1 UCLA, No. 2 Wake Forest and No. 3 Texas. The Bruins and Longhorns are the only programs to ink a pair of top-10 signings while the Demon Deacons will bring in No. 1 Amelia Zalsman as an early enrollee this spring. item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. item.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
item.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. item.title: Film review: What Josh Downs brings to the Chiefs’ offense
item.description: (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Christmas came early this year for Kansas City Chiefs fans asking for a wide receiver. Before the trade deadline on Tuesday, general manager Brett Veach struck a deal with the Indianapolis Colts for receiver Josh Downs. The 25-year-old playmaker has the skill set to be one of quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ top weapons. This season, Downs was the Colts’ leading receiver by yards (354), more yards than any Chiefs pass catcher besides tight end Travis Kelce (482). Through three weeks, Downs was on pace for a career season (62 yards per game), but the Colts quickly went into fire-sale mode amid a lost season. This is reflected in his most recent production. The fourth-year wideout — a former third-round pick — was ready for a change of scenery, and there’s reason to believe Kansas City will be a good place to maximize his talents. Let’s take a closer look at why that’s the case: Getting open quickly In his NFL career, Downs has played nearly 80% of his pass-play snaps aligned in the slot, according to Pro Football Focus . He is constantly used to win on quick-hitting routes, showing off route-running chops against man coverage and the elusiveness to find creases in zone coverage. His ability to win against man coverage is arguably the biggest reason he will make a difference for the Chiefs’ offense the rest of the year. On this play, he runs an option route and stays patient coming off the line, reading the defense’s movement. He identifies the vacancy over the middle and makes a decisive move to create separation. These option routes have not been as common in the Chiefs’ offense, especially with a wide receiver. In his prime, Travis Kelce ran these routes very well, but it takes the right combination of physical and mental tools to make them a constant play call. In general, Downs will be a reliable option on short throws because of his feel for spacing on his routes and toughness after the catch. He has urgency to turn upfield, which helps him slip off tacklers; he runs hard and purposefully for his stature (5 feet 9 inches tall and 171 pounds at the 2023 NFL Scouting Combine). item.title: Mizzou football still has much to play for
item.description: If there’s one thing Mizzou fans probably don’t want to do right now, it’s think about the Texas game. I’ve spent enough time replaying that one in my head, and, judging by the Twittersphere, I’m not alone among my Mizzou brethren. That game was a gut punch; the kind of loss that makes it tempting to write off the rest of the year, declare it all meaningless, convert to nihilism and start looking ahead to 2027 (or at least basketball season.) As tempting as that may be for Tigers fans, it would certainly be a mistake if the team took that same approach. Mizzou still has three games left, and while the College Football Playoff path has gotten awfully narrow, it hasn’t disappeared entirely. Winning out, however unlikely, would include victories over two top-15 opponents and would at least keep Mizzou in the conversation for one of the final spots in the 12-team field. There is no getting around the dissatisfaction (and really, let’s be honest, the resentment) of how the Texas game played out. But even if the playoff dream doesn’t come together, there are plenty of reasons to care about what happens over the next three weeks. In fact, Mizzou has quite a bit more to play for than just a long-shot postseason bid. Being realistic, the Tigers probably need a whole heap of help to get into the playoff at this point. A loss to Texas took away the margin for error, and the remaining schedule offers zero room to stumble. A road trip to face the AP No. 1 Georgia Bulldogs is not exactly an ideal place to start a winning streak. Taking a quick trip into pipe dream land for a bit: Winning all three would give the Tigers an 9-3 record with victories over two top-15 opponents. That would at least put them in position to make a case for one of the final at-large spots, depending on how the rest of the season shakes out. The important thing is that the opportunity still exists. The Tigers don’t have to spend the next three weeks scoreboard watching or wondering what might have been. They can make a statement by taking care of their own business, starting with an enormous challenge in Athens. Chasing history Even if the playoff is a long shot, Mizzou has a pretty significant program milestone within reach. The Tigers have two more home games after Georgia, against opponents that are more than beatable. Winning two of the final three would give Mizzou at least eight victories for the fourth consecutive season under Eli Drinkwitz. In the 136-year history of the program, Mizzou has only had one other stretch where it has put together a run of at least four consecutive eight-win seasons: Gary Pinkel’s teams did it six years in a row from 2006–2011. Drinkwitz has already established a level of consistency that has been difficult for this program to sustain historically. item.description: Shaker celebrates after beating Guilderland for the Section 2, Class AAA title on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026, at LaSalle Institute in Troy, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) LATHAM - Braddigan Lanfear was a sophomore called up from junior varsity when Shaker coach Dan Fountain told him to warm up in the 2024 Class AAA boys' soccer state final. "That was the craziest thing I've ever heard," Lanfear recalled. He got to his feet, got ready, and played six minutes with a state title on the line. He admits much of the game was "kind of a blur," but he remembers how it ended. Shaker led Fairport 1-0 before losing 2-1 in overtime. Two years later, Lanfear and goalkeeper Alex Cross are senior starters on a Shaker team that's one win away from another shot at a state title. The Blue Bison face Section 6's Lancaster in Friday's Class AAA state semifinal in Middletown, drawing on lessons from the loss to Fairport and last fall's abrupt end to an unbeaten season. Shaker went 13-0-4 last year but was eliminated by Guilderland in the sectional semifinals on penalty kicks. Lanfear remembers how nervous he was for that game. He also remembers the tears after Shaker's season ended. "Now I'm just excited for every game," Lanfear said. Cross had been called up as a backup goalkeeper for sectionals as a freshman and again as a sophomore in 2024. From the bench in the state final, he watched Shaker shift into a defensive mindset after taking the lead against Fairport. This fall, Cross said, Shaker has worked to play its game for the full 80 minutes, staying aggressive when it takes a lead instead of getting protective. "Don't get complacent when you go up," he said. "Try to stay composed." This season, the Blue Bison have also learned how to respond when they fall behind. They opened with losses to John Jay, Scarsdale and Shenendehowa as players adjusted to bigger roles. Cross said those games gave Shaker experience in staying calm when it conceded early. The two postseason exits already pushed the returning players to work harder in the offseason, Fountain said. But the 0-3 start showed them where they still needed to improve and Shaker (14-6) responded by winning eight straight and earning the top seed in sectionals. "You learn a lot through failure, and these boys embraced those first three games and the lessons from them very well, and really built upon that," Fountain said. In the regional final against Section 3's Cicero-North Syracuse, Shaker again had a 1-0 lead to protect. With about a minute left, Cross spotted an opponent drifting toward the back post and called a winger back to cover. He also made a save in the final seconds to preserve the shutout and send the Blue Bison back to the state semifinals. "It felt like all our hard work over the years was finally paying off," Cross said. item.title: Winners and losers from the NFL trade deadline
item.description: The deadline is done, and NFL rosters are more or less set for the remainder of the season. We didn’t get an earth-shattering buzzer-beater that will reshape the league, but some pretty significant deals took place which will impact the race to the playoffs. Making deals at the trade deadline is always a fascinating push-and-pull. Teams need to balance confidence in their ability to compete right now with potentially sacrificing too much down the road, should things not pan out. Look at the Indianapolis Colts ad the cautionary tale, who are stuck regretting their deal for Sauce Gardner this time last year. Indy gave up two first-round picks with the belief they were just a piece away, and now they’re stuck rebuilding without a top draft asset. This year’s biggest buyers were the Jacksonville Jaguars, and they went big. The team landed S Jessie Bates from the Falcons for a second, added Davon Godchaux to bolster their defensive line, and in the biggest trade of the deadline they made a deal for run-stopping DT Jordan Davis from the Eagles. The vision is that this team just wants to stop a few more drives per game, confident that their stellar offense can win enough games. Let’s swing around the league to look at who won the deadline, and who made some questionable moves. Winner: Kirk Cousins and the Vikings The biggest winner on the Vikings’ side of the ledger was Kirk Cousins, who had been vocal about wanting to return to Minnesota. The veteran QB achieved exactly what was asked of him in Las Vegas, basically being a veteran mentor to Fernando Mendoza and stewarding the first part of the season. Now the Raiders can turn the keys over to Mendoza to begin getting him some live-fire reps, while Cousins will move on with a chance to actually compete for a Super Bowl ring — rather than awkwardly holding a clipboard for the final months of the season. Kudos to Minnesota for giving it their best shot. A third-round pick for Cousins is more than they probably should have spent, but there was absolutely no other option for them. The entire league knew they were desperate and made sure to put the screws to them. The good news for Vikings fans is that the team didn’t mortage the entire future of this run, meaning this was a good half-step between a potential home run trade, and a mediocre one that wouldn’t have changed anything. Loser: Kyler Murray This was a one-year prove-it deal for Murray in Minnesota, and he sucked out loud. There is zero chance he will land another starting job in the NFL next season, with his best option to turn into a veteran journeyman like Jameis Winston as a high-level backup QB. item.description: Giants manager Tony Vitello, seen after the season, has been on a whirlwind tour of visits to players, coaches and sporting events. (Stephen Lam/S.F. Chronicle) LAS VEGAS - Since the San Francisco Giants ' season ended, Tony Vitello hasn't gone one week without getting on an airplane. And he may not stop moving until the baseball season begins - whenever that may be, pending a lockout. Vitello went back to his old stomping grounds in Knoxville to watch the Tennessee football team bully Alabama, and on Halloween night was just feet away from head coach Lincoln Riley on the USC football sideline when they beat Ohio State. Between college game days he took a breather with friends in Carmel, where the gang would trek during their days coaching in Salinas. Last week Vitello was parked in the Seattle Seahawks' suite, secretly rooting for his Chicago Bears on Monday night. Two days later he was roaming the Golden State Valkyries ' championship parade in San Francisco. He flew to Arizona and camped out at Papago to watch prospects and big leaguers alike get back on the field; for those in their hometowns, Vitello has a list of players he'll visit individually. First on that list was a trip to New York to see outfielder Harrison Bader , whose pay the Giants suspended when he got into a late-night scooter crash in San Francisco's Marina District. Bader played just 30 games in 2026, dealing with plantar fasciitis that the accident worsened. "I don't mean to speak too much for him, but I also don't mind saying, I think he feels a sense of duty," Vitello said, just before the general managers meetings kicked off at the Aria Resort & Casino in Las Vegas. "Last year didn't go the way he wanted performance-wise when he was on the field, and no player wants to be injured. And I think he's in a pretty good head space for how motivated he is going into next year. "I think a lot of guys have a little bit of a chip on their shoulder based off last year - for different reasons." Count Vitello among those with a chip. Around this time last year, the Giants made history by hiring Vitello straight out of the college ranks. His first year at the helm was turbulent, just as the Giants' season was; the team lost 97 games and looked out of sorts from the jump as Vitello navigated the realities of managing a professional baseball team. As the team plummeted, his decision-making came under scrutiny and his long-winded explanations lacked the clarity to get the spotlight off his back. How a Giants team built to contend spiraled into a near-historically bad season boils down to a basic conclusion from Vitello and those up top: The team just needs to play better baseball and prevent more runs. The 2026 season flew off the rails because no one was truly on the same page on Opening Day. Abstractly, that kind of directive puts an onus on its leaders in the front office and in the clubhouse. item.description: BALTIMORE, MD - AUGUST 21: Andrew Kittredge #39 of the Baltimore Orioles looks on after pitching against the Tampa Bay Rays during the eighth inning at Oriole Park at Camden Yards on August 21, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Orioles’ decision to reacquire Andrew Kittredge from the Chicago Cubs was their first attempt at reshaping the 2026 O’s into a contender. And, like many of the Orioles’ efforts in 2026, it turned out to be a little misguided as Kittredge’s second run in Baltimore had more lows than highs. Baltimore purchased Kittredge’s contract from the Cubs on November 4th, 2025. The move brought the veteran reliever back to Baltimore just over three months after Mike Elias sent him to Chicago at the 2025 trade deadline. At the time, it looked like a stroke of genius from the Orioles front office. In sending Kittredge to Chicago, the Orioles brought back teenage SS propsect Wilfri De La Cruz (now Baltimore’s No. 30 prospect). To be able to buy the 36-year-old right-hander back for cash considerations just months later gave the Orioles a way to bolster their bullpen at virtually no cost. With the Orioles also adding veteran closer Ryan Helsley last offseason, the assumption was that Kittredge would slot into the 7th/8th inning role for Baltimore. That plan was put on hold to begin the year, as he started on the IL with right shoulder inflammation. When he finally made his 2026 debut on April 24th, he slotted right back into that set up role, working a scoreless 7th inning in a win against the Red Sox. Over the next month, eight of his 13 appearances came in the 7th or 8th innings. If you ignore a May 3rd blow up against the Yankees that saw him give up seven runs while only recording one out, Kittredge pitched to a 1.74 ERA over his first 12 appearances of the season. Over those same outings, he racked up 12 Ks across 10.1 innings while allowing a .179 batting average against. By all accounts, his return to the Orioles as a set up man was going according to plan. Kittredge’s role changed as it became clear that Helsley couldn’t stay healthy. Though the Orioles would-be closer first landed on the IL on May 1st, it wasn’t until June that Kittredge started consistently getting the call in the 9th inning. From the beginning of June until the All-Star break, the veteran righty made nine of his 16 appearances in the 9th inning. item.title: Spalletti Leading Juventus to Historically Slow Start
item.description: Spalletti Leading Juventus to Historically Slow Start Luciano Spalletti strengthened his grip on the Juventus bench by beating Napoli convincingly, but he and the team were unable to build on it, dropping two more points against Fiorentina a week later. The Bianconeri have yet to prevail in back-to-back Serie A matches. They were unable to take advantage of a pair of big games elsewhere to close the gap. According to La Gazzetta dello Sport , the Old Lady had started this slowly just twice in the last 20 years. In 2015/2016, when they staged had an incredible comeback, ripping off a 15-game winning streak and winning the Scudetto. Then, in 2021/2022, when they sprinted late to qualify for the UEFA Champions League. Juventus currently sit six points behind Milan, with Como and Frosinone in between. They hadn’t been this poor early even in their worst seasons in recent history, with Ciro Ferrara, Alberto Zaccheroni and Luigi Delneri in their dugout. A year ago, they had done marginally better at this stage of the competition, picking up 19 points, but they were closer to their rivals. They already have a double-digit gap from first place. If they don’t improve their current point average, 1.64, their projected tally would at most suffice for a sixth- or seventh-placed finish. Our Take on Juventus and Spalletti It’s been groundhog day, as they have had strong displays only against small teams or when the sky was falling and the coach seemed on the verge of getting the boot, prompting decent reactions. They have been hit hard by injuries, but that’s not an acceptable way to go. Plus, they are rarely in control of matches, given their deficiencies on both ends.
